claim: China's suspension of critical-minerals export controls (rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony, graphite general licenses for US end users) is not extended past its 2026-11-10 expiry on the same or looser terms; controls lapse, are reinstated, or are tightened (broader item scope or stricter end-use review).
resolution_rule: YES if by 2026-12-31 MOFCOM has announced reinstatement or tightening of the suspended measures, or has let the suspension lapse with no extension announced. NO if MOFCOM announces a formal extension of the suspension on the same or looser terms. Source: MOFCOM announcements (mofcom.gov.cn), cross-checked with law-firm updates (Pillsbury, Clark Hill).
notes: Memo called late-2026 reinstatement the dominant downside scenario and extension-dependent plans the most regret-likely posture; 60% derived from that stance. Bootstrapped from the 2026-05-08 memo; outcome not checked at logging.

claim: The European Commission publishes at least one CBAM methodology adjustment (updated default values or a scope refinement) for the definitive regime within 12 months of 2026-05-08.
resolution_rule: YES if the Commission publishes updated CBAM default values or a scope/methodology refinement dated between 2026-05-08 and 2027-05-08 (Official Journal or the Commission CBAM page). NO otherwise. Source: European Commission CBAM publications (taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu).
indicator: Commission CBAM default-value and methodology updates
notes: Memo stated flatly that carbon-leakage and trade-friction concerns will produce ongoing methodology adjustments over 12 months; 80% = lower bound of 'very likely'. About half the window had already elapsed at logging; outcome not checked at logging.

claim: The EU AI Act synthetic-content transparency obligations under the 2026-05-07 provisional agreement take effect with the 3-month grace period ending 2026-12-02 intact, without further postponement.
resolution_rule: YES if by 2026-12-15 the agreement has been formally adopted (Council and Parliament) and the 2026-12-02 synthetic-content transparency deadline stands. NO if adoption fails or the deadline is postponed. Source: EUR-Lex / Official Journal and European Commission AI Act pages.
indicator: EUR-Lex adoption status of the AI Act simplification package
notes: Memo treats the December 2026 transparency deadline as operative and warns against reading the deal as a haircut; 70% = 'likely'. Part of the window had elapsed at logging; outcome not checked at logging.

claim: EU or UK regulators (EBA, FCA, or equivalents) update typology-based supervisory expectations on Iranian sanctions-evasion networks in response to OFAC's SB-0477 typology disclosure, within roughly two quarters of 2026-05-08.
resolution_rule: YES if the EBA, FCA, or an equivalent EU/UK supervisor publishes typology guidance or a bulletin responding to the OFAC SB-0477 Zarringhalam-network typologies by 2026-11-30. NO otherwise. Source: EBA and FCA publication feeds.
notes: Memo said 'likely in the next 1-2 quarters'; 65% = 'likely'. Window effectively closed at logging; outcome deliberately not checked at logging to keep the record honest.

claim: Kyrgyzstan's VASP sector comes under formal external FATF scrutiny: Kyrgyzstan is named in FATF's targeted virtual-asset review (results due June and October 2027) as a jurisdiction with materially important VA activity, or is placed on the FATF increased-monitoring list.
resolution_rule: YES if by 2027-10-31 FATF publishes the targeted VA review naming Kyrgyzstan, or adds Kyrgyzstan to the increased-monitoring (grey) list. NO otherwise. Source: fatf-gafi.org plenary outcomes, targeted review publications, and public statements.
indicator: FATF targeted VA review and grey-list publications
notes: Memo: the October 2026 plenary acceleration decision 'raises the odds of formal external scrutiny' and 'could put the Kyrgyz VASP sector under formal external monitoring by 2027'; 45% = 'roughly even chance', low end.

claim: CPC (Novorossiysk) remains the export route for the majority of Kazakhstan's crude over the 12 months from 2026-05-08; diversification via BTC, Aktau, Atyrau-Samara and Atasu-Alashankou stays small in absolute terms.
resolution_rule: YES if CPC's share of Kazakhstani crude exports exceeds 50% for full-year 2026 per Kazakhstan energy ministry or CPC reporting. NO if alternative routes collectively carry more than CPC. Source: official KZ statistics / CPC annual reporting.
notes: Memo: ~80% of KZ crude via CPC in 2024, concentration persisted since CPC commissioning, alternatives small; 90% = 'very likely'. Part of the window had elapsed at logging; outcome not checked at logging.
